content: Methylcellulose is an over-the-counter (OTC) laxative that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of constipation. It is commonly used to help restore and maintain regular bowel movements and to relieve constipation, including cases associated with other bowel disorders such as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), when recommended by a healthcare provider. Typically, it produces a bowel movement within 12 to 72 hours after administration. When taking methylcellulose, it is essential to consume it with at least 8 ounces (a full glass) of water or another fluid. Failure to take the product with sufficient liquid may result in choking, as the product can swell and obstruct the throat or esophagus. Individuals who experience chest pain, vomiting, or difficulty swallowing or breathing after taking the product should seek immediate medical attention. Methylcellulose is contraindicated in individuals who have difficulty swallowing. Patients are advised to consult a doctor before use if they experience a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks, abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting. If constipation persists for more than seven days or if rectal bleeding occurs, the use of the product should be discontinued, and medical advice should be sought, as these symptoms may indicate a more serious condition. The most common adverse reactions associated with methylcellulose include flatulence and abdominal distension. In rare cases, intestinal obstruction may occur. There is limited information available regarding postmarketing adverse events, drug interactions, and off-label uses of methylcellulose. Methylcellulose is classified as a bulk-forming fiber laxative. Each caplet contains 500 mg of methylcellulose, along with other inactive ingredients such as crospovidone, dibasic calcium phosphate, FD&C yellow no. 6 aluminum lake, magnesium stearate, maltodextrin, povidone, and sodium lauryl sulfate. Each caplet also provides 10 mg of calcium. There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of methylcellulose in pregnant or nursing women, pediatric or geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no guidance on its use in specific gender or racial populations, immunocompromised patients, or individuals of reproductive potential. Methylcellulose is administered orally. It should be stored at temperatures below 77°F (25°C) and protected from humidity. The container should be kept tightly closed to maintain product integrity. The product is marketed under the brand name CITRUCEL®, which is a registered trademark of the Sanofi group of companies and licensed by the GlaxoSmithKline group of companies. It is promoted as a gentle and clinically proven effective fiber therapy for regularity that does not cause excess gas. For additional information or patient counseling, individuals can call the toll-free number provided on the product label.
